subject: A question about Probabilistic Selection Task results

messages.author: ebb1ab0c02004eee
messages.subject: A question about Probabilistic Selection Task results
parts:
Hello! 

Thank you for this awesome program! Its helping a lot with my research. I have a question regarding results from running the probabilistic selection task model. 

The resulting alpha_pos, alpha_neg, and beta values across my sample are fairly homogenous. For example, in my sample of 90 people, the mean alpha positive is 0.35144 with a standard deviation of just 0.0009644. Is this little variability normal? Does it suggest that should change one of the options in running the model? 

If its any help, looking at my task performance data, there is more variability in participant choice accuracy during training (mean accuracy = 50.34% and SD of 4.61%). I'd appreciate any guidance you can provide! 

Best, 
Jenny

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: A question about Probabilistic Selection Task results
parts:
Hi Jenny,

Thanks for the question!

That is indeed a low level of variation across participants. Have the chains converged? Sometimes such low variation arises when chains get stuck.

Alternatively, it could be that the variation across subjects is indeed low. Usually, if there are estimation problems, the chains will get stuck at a parameter bound and will not take on typical values (alpha of .35 is pretty typical for these tasks). Have you looked at the individual posterior distributions? You can use plotInd(my_fit, pars = ‘alpha_pos’, show_density = T) to visually check them.
Best,
Nate

messages.subject: Re: A question about Probabilistic Selection Task results
parts:
Ah yes, it looks like the chains are stuck up against the bound. It is difficult to say what is going on for sure without knowing more about your data—could you possibly share a small subset of your data? Or even more information on the specific task you are using? 

This can sometimes happen due to problems with data formatting, but other times it just indicates that the model is not well-suited for the data.

messages.author: ebb1ab0c02004eee
messages.subject: Re: A question about Probabilistic Selection Task results
parts:
Hi Nate!

Great, thank you for helping me get to the bottom of this - my data file is attached. The columns as as follows: subjID, type (image stimuli), choice (0 = incorrect, 1 = correct), reward (0 = punish, 1 = reward). Each row corresponds to 1 trial. 

Task details are as follows: 
Participants complete the PST while undergoing an fMRI scan. On any given trial, they were shown two stimuli on the screen and asked to select which stim they though was "correct". They had 2 seconds to make their selection, and then received feedback in the form of tastes delivered into their mouth via long flexible plastic tubing that connected to beverage dispensers outside the magnet. When they chose correctly, they received a pleasurable, sweet taste, when they chose incorrectly, they received an aversive, bitter taste. If they did not chose, they did not receive a reinforcer, and the trial was not considered complete. Because of this, each participant has a variable number of complete trials. During the scan they saw three pairs of images: the 80-20 reinforced pair (stimuli 1 is correct 80%, stimuli 2 is correct 20%), the 70-30 reinforced pair (stimuli 3 is correct 70%, stimuli 4 is correct 30%), and the 60-40 reinforced pair (stimuli 5 is correct 60%, stimuli 6 is correct 40%). The pair presented was randomly determined by the paradigm (run in PsychoPy). Generally, we tried to map our paradigm as closely to the original Frank task.
